utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case IT-08-91-T, the Prosecutor versus Mico Stanisic and Stojan Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Good morning to everyone. May we have the appearances, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. For the Prosecution, I'm Tom Hannis, along with Alex Demirdjian, and our Case Manager today is Indah Susanti.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Slobodan Zecevic, Slobodan Cvijetic, Eugene O'Sullivan, and Ms. Tatjana Savic appearing for Stanisic Defence this morning. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Nothing heard in the channel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: May the witness be escorted back to the stand, if there's nothing we need concern ourselves with. The -- could we have the appearance again in respect of the Stanisic Defence because nothing came through on the channel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The microphone is not working. The counsel should use another microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALEKSIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Aleksandar Aleksic appearing for Zupljanin Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: It seems to have come through now. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, good morning to you, sir, for, what we trust will the last time. I give you the usual reminder of your solemn declaration before I ask Mr. Zecevic to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, yesterday, towards the end, we spoke about P5530 [as interpreted], and that was the Law on Internal Affairs of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. And the topic we discussed was assistance.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P530.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During examination-in-chief, page -- or, rather, during cross-examination, page 20935 and onwards, you were answering questions from Ms. Korner. That's when you commented on Articles ^ 27 and 31 of this law. That is page 4 in the Serbian language.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What I would like to hear about from you are some examples for the application of Article 27. It says that the public security station shall implement regulation passed by the municipal assembly, relating to law and order and road safety. Mr. Bjelosevic, a decision by the municipal assembly, whereby cafes are supposed to close, say, at 2300 hours, is that one such regulation, as mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A decision by municipal assembly prescribing that cafes serving alcohol may not open before noon, for instance. Is that another example of such a regulation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Municipal assembly decisions regulate precisely those kind of issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A decision by municipal assembly that certain segments of the road shall have speed limits because of the proximity to a school or hospital, is that another example of such regulation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It is the jurisdiction of the municipal assembly to decide and mark such places in town and on the roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If, for instance, the Visegrad Municipal Assembly decides to ban the traffic across the Drina River bridge, the old monumental bridge, is that another example of a regulation stipulated by this article of this law?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So these are my examples. Are these examples representatives -- representative for Article 27 of this Law on Internal Affairs and the kind of regulations envisaged there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is public security station duty-bound to enforce such regulations, in accordance with this article?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can a municipal assembly adopt regulations pertaining to - if you know, that is - can a municipal assembly adopt regulations pertaining to matters that are already regulated by another law?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that, in principle, they can go into details, in accordance with that law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us take another example. If the Law on Internal Affairs defines measures and authority of the officials of internal affairs and the circumstances under which such authorities may be used, accompanied by force, is it then possible for a municipal assembly to change what has been defined by the Law on Internal Affairs by its own regulation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If a municipal assembly were to adopt a regulation contrary to the Law on Internal Affairs which regulates your authority, is then a public security station duty-bound to enforce such regulation?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let us now turn to Article 31.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the next page of the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Bjelosevic, Article 31 defines the obligation of CSB and public security station to provide reports and information, if so requested by the municipal assembly and the executive committee. Is this sort of reporting a replacement for your regular reports that are sent to the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is the so-called horizontal reporting that goes towards municipal organs. Those informations are copied to them, so that they would be informed. It's for your information. And as for the flow of information towards the ministry, in its entirety, and according to lines of work, that is something that is defined by the hierarchical structure.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, let us take another example. Municipal assembly requests public security station, or the Doboj CSB, to inform them about the situation with crime in the municipality, particularly relating to narcotics. Is then the Security Services Centre, in accordance with this request, duty-bound to provide this information?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This article is quite precise. All the information, all the events relating to the area of a particular municipality, yes. In such a case, they have a duty to provide such information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, this Article 31 that is something that imposes a duty to the public security station, or the Security Services Centre to provide information upon request by municipal organs. Does it impose this -- does it impose a duty, as well, to enact an order that you might receive from the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it relates to the areas in which municipal assembly may enact its regulation as bylaws.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you refer to the articles mentioned in Article 27?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I had in mind. So if it's something in relation to such decisions, decisions that fall within the jurisdiction of the municipal assembly, then, yes, they're duty-bound to enact them.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In order to clarify this issue, we should take a look at Article 32. Mr. Bjelosevic, let us stay with the example that I've just given. It's a hypothetical. Municipal organs of the Doboj municipality are concerned about the rise in substance abuse among underage persons, for instance, in schools. They request a report from the CSB in which the CSB has to describe the situation with crime, in accordance with Article 31, and in such report, you confirm their concerns. That, indeed, the number of offences committed by underage persons related to substance abuse is, indeed, on the rise. In such a case, the municipal assembly wants to introduce some measures, and they say, We request the Security Services Centre to increase the number of operatives in charge of this particular crime, this particular kind of crime. We want them to control and prevent substance abuse in schools and other institutions. Is it then possible -- should the municipal assembly, in accordance -- in accordance with Article 32, forward this kind of proposal to the ministry for their additional consideration?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If they propose some additional activities, or changes in the normal course of work, then they should put it in writing as a proposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When this proposal is considered in the ministry, and when it is found to be justified there are reasons for the ministry to undertake certain steps in relation to that, is the ministry then duty-bound to issue to you an order, directive, or instruction for you to act in accordance with it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If there are any change in the organisation of work, they have to issue such an instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So, this kind of a report -- this kind of a request submitted by the municipal assembly or the municipal organs should go, first of all, to the ministry, and if it is accepted by the ministry, only then should be sent to the CSB, and only then is the Security Services Centre duty-bound to enact it in accordance with the order that comes from the ministry.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A decision or a request by municipal assembly or its organs that does not follow this procedure but goes directly from the municipal assembly to the Security Services Centre, or public security station, without the ministry being consulted, is that kind of directive or instruction then something that imposes a duty on the Security Services Centre to act?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I don't know whether it's a case of Mr. Hannis exercising extraordinary restraint, but apart from the ordinary -- the minimal utility on propositions beginning with "if", because, of course, that can be unending, the last series of -- the -- coming back to -- I'm surprised Mr. Hannis hasn't challenged you for making a speech instead of asking questions. I don't know what usefulness the last set of exchanges has been, in terms of the -- what the witness is saying. Could you assist us by focussing on the -- exactly how you relate to the articles to the practice on the ground?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I was trying to do that by giving the examples. That's why I was using the "ifs" in a hypothetical meaning. But I will -- I will -- I will ask the witness to -- to explain his position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, the CSB, or the SJB, actually, is it duty-bound to implement the decisions of municipal bodies that are -- or -- that are not covered by Articles 27, 31, and 32 of the Law on Internal Affairs?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Only if subordinate legislation is in accordance with the law, then, yes; but, otherwise, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, let's take a look at something else. During your cross-examination, you commented your diary for Ms. Korner on more than one occasion.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have one here. Perhaps you're referring to that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think it was returned and it is currently with the Registrar.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner showed you document 65 ter 20103. That's in the Prosecution tab 107B. It's about your diary entry dated 10 March 1992. You confirmed to Ms. Korner that this is about a meeting held in Bosanski Brod; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We'll return to this later because I now cannot find the reference in the transcript, so I'll move on to my next question. Mr. Bjelosevic, you commented your diary and the entries made in late December in the context of Stevan Todorovic, chief of the Samac SJB; do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D518.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, is this your dispatch dated 25 November 1992, and tell us what it is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is a dispatch that I sent to the ministry or to the minister, rather, with a request to replace Stevan Todorovic from the position of chief of the SJB, and I pointed out that Stevan Todorovic was never appointed pursuant to a decision of the minister or anybody else from the ministry, and that for that reason, disciplinary proceedings cannot be instituted against him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned disciplinary proceedings, you will remember that Ms. Korner and the Trial Chamber had some questions about this. Tell me, Mr. Bjelosevic, under the Law on Internal Affairs and subordinate legislation regulating these matters, against who can disciplinary proceedings be instituted?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Against such persons who are lawfully employed with some body or institution. Which means, in practice, that the person in question was appointed by virtue of a decision of the official in charge. Disciplinary proceedings can be instituted against such persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To be completely clear, let me ask you: Can disciplinary proceedings be instituted only against MUP members who are employed with the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I believe that's what I said in my previous answer. Only in such a case can -- are disciplinary proceedings possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We have seen that the MUP also has a reserve police force. Can disciplinary proceedings be launched against reserve police members?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Disciplinary proceedings are not possible in that case. The person in question can only be deleted from the list of reserve police members. Their wartime assignment is cancelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You said "wartime assignment." When you say that, you mean their wartime assignment as members of the reserve police.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's what we're talking about, the reserve police force.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 1D520, just for a brief comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, is this your dispatch dated 27 November? And why did you send this dispatch to the minister and the commander of the special police brigade?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Again, I'm operating at a handicap. But I'm not sure where in the cross-examination this stems from. If I could have a reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, I cannot give you a page reference now because by mistake or -- as a consequence of an update of the transcript, we lost the exact page references. But my question refers to the 23rd of May, Ms. Korner's cross-examination about Stevan Todorovic on pages 19 through 25 of that day's transcript, and then pages 27 through 33. I don't know if this is sufficient for your purposes. I cannot give you a more exact reference, but it's basically a technical problem. I'm being informed that the pages are 21097. That's the beginning of Ms. Korner's examination concerning Stevan Todorovic. May I continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, my question was whether this is your document, what the date is, and what the reason was for drafting and sending out this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a dispatch that I sent out, and the reason, as stated here, is the aggravated security situation in the Samac municipality, which ensued after the arrest of the then-station chief Todorovic, and the president of the Executive Board of Bosanski Samac, Mr. Simic. Then the president of the municipality ordered that the passage through the corridor shall be blocked. That was why I requested additional forces, because I wanted to stabilise the situation and put things under control.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On transcript page 33 of that day -- I'm not sure now but it's probably 21990 or some such. Anyway, you commented on your audit of some documents which you conducted as CSB chief. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, could you give me more detail to jog my memory?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner put to you that some documents that are routinely kept by a CSB or, rather, an SJB, you never saw at the Samac SJB.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember the question. But that's not a task of the chief of the centre but a task of the inspectors, according to their respective lines of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document 1D519. The page reference is 21.117 of the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, sir, do you know this document? Who is Mirko Blazanovic and what is this document about? We can see the signatures on page 3, so possibly you can authenticate the document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This document was drafted after an audit of the Samac SJB and signed by the then-chief of the department of the police at the Doboj CSB, Mirko Blazanovic. And his team conducted the audit and drafted this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry. Your Honours, I need to interrupt. The question was: Can you authenticate the document. He has done that. And the document is already in evidence, as I understand it, and this seems to be a re-hash of the direct testimony of the witness on this point. I'm not sure how it arises from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just in all fairness to the witness, I wanted to show him the signature at the end. I know it's -- it's already admitted document, so, therefore, I'm not trying to re-hash his direct evidence. The question which was posed by Ms. Korner refers to the inspections, the -- of the -- of the CSB Doboj in -- in -- in Samac SJB and that is precisely what I want to discuss with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I believe that was already discussed in direct examination, and I don't see anything new arising from cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, the suggestion during the cross-examination by Ms. Korner was that it was for the witness to -- that the witness should have gone to the inspection of the -- of the SJB of Bosanski Samac. Than is the only thing I want to discuss.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And on cross-examination, the witness said no, it wasn't his job. It was the job of the inspectors. So I don't know that it needs any further clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, let's move on, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 285D1. That is tab 208.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us what this is all about. Is this your document; and could you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a document of the CSB Doboj and I signed it. This is a cover letter, accompanying the report of the working group for coordination of the SJB Bosanski Samac. It is sent to the ministry, to the administration for police duties and assignments.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Was it only after this report about the work for coordination -- the work of the group for coordination that a decision could be made about replacing Stevan Todorovic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I be allowed only two sentences about what was found, inter alia, during this inspection?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honours, that's not the question.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] I would request -- that you direct the witness to answer the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bjelosevic, could you confine yourself to answering the question posed by counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was only after this inspection and after this information was written up that a dispatch was sent. If I remember correctly, even to the president of the republic, all for the purpose of having Chief Todorovic replaced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, for what it is worth, it's a cover letter. It's not the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: How does this assist, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the suggestion by Ms. Korner to the witness was that, even in December 1992, Stevan Todorovic, despite the knowledge of the -- of the witness and at that point, relatively public knowledge of what Mr. Todorovic did during the 1992, when he was chief of the SJB Samac, he wasn't replaced by the end of 1992. And that is precisely why I want to introduce this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could somebody remind me as to whether the report is in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I believe this -- the report which I showed to the witness before, which is 1D519, is the report which -- which is -- which is sent with this letter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So the -- why do we need the cover letter or is it merely for completion?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Because of the date. Because the report itself does not have a date, 1D519. And now this cover letter shows -- [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I follow you Mr. Zecevic. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... Your Honour, there's not a date on the report. How do we know that that report is the one that's attached to this cover letter?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Because of the witness's testimony is the short answer. Wouldn't it be?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I guess I wasn't here to see him say that. But Mr. Zecevic said this was because of the suggestion by Ms. Korner that the witness, even in December 1992, had not been removed. I'd like to have a transcript reference to where Ms. Korner made that suggestion. From what I have been able to glance over, it appears that she was saying he wasn't removed even up until 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: If we can separate the arguments for the evidence, Mr. Hannis, it seems, that, as Mr. Zecevic has said, the relevance of this cover letter is to put a date to the report that's already in evidence. So it's for that limited it -- with that understanding. I see no difficulty of it being admitted. Now, in terms of the rest of what you have said, Mr. Hannis, that's a matter for argument. Yes, so the letter is -- letter/note is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D544, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As a matter of curiosity, Mr. Zecevic, in my part of the world and I suppose it holds true here as well, that a lawyer's minute is not exactly what it is by the clock. I see that you're 53 minutes into the 30 minutes that you indicated that you would be when we adjourned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, it was a misunderstanding, Your Honours, that -- I requested, I was hoping to finish yesterday within 30 minutes, and then I said that it would not be possible, and, therefore, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. I thought I misunderstood you, because I thought when we took the adjournment you indicated that you would be 30 minutes longer than you thought you would have been.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, I am afraid not, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I see. We proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, Ms. Korner asked a number of questions about these payment lists and documents. I have prepared these documents for you so that you can give us your brief comment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please be assisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Can I have a reference in the transcript where this topic was addressed so I can follow along.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21037 is the transcript reference.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Zecevic. Ah, it came out on the transcript -- now I have it. 21037?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown P1346. That is Prosecution tab 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, you do remember that Ms. Korner showed you this document, and your comment was that you were unfamiliar with the document, if I remember correctly.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, and on the basis of what you see before you, can you tell us about the provenance of this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not recognise the signatures. Probably from the station? The Public Security Station Doboj, I assume.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, the witness has said he doesn't recognise the signatures. And the document I see on the screen doesn't appear to have any signatures but one. Is he talking about the same document I'm looking at?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, he is talking about the same document. The document which is on the screen has two signatures. If they can be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are two signatures.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't see the one under this signature -- this seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document that I wish to show you is 65 ter - it's a Prosecution document - 20113, tab 26B. I have been informed that it is now P2328. Sir, you remember that Ms. Korner showed you this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In order to have a perfectly clear transcript, can you tell us whether you recognise the signature on page 5 of this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obren Petrovic, chief of the SJB; it's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In your view, is this a document of the public security station of Doboj or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no doubt. If it was signed by the chief of the station, then it is a document of the public security station Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The next document that I wish to show you is P1338; Prosecution tab 14F. Mr. Bjelosevic, you remember that this document was also shown to you by Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at the first eight pages of this document and give us your comment with regard to this document. The first eight pages. 20.0007. The ERN number is that -- of that particular page.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, all of these eight pages or, rather, seven pages of text, do they all have two seals, a big one and a small one? And, if so, can you tell us what they are?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The big seal was made, I cannot remember exactly when, I think it was sometime in July, and these lists for payment were made retroactively, because in the month of April, the employees who worked there did not receive a salary. They were supposed to receive a salary from the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. Because of everything that happened, in terms of war developments, that had not been done. In order to regulate everything that had to do with employees, this was done as I said already, and I point that out again, the amounts were minimal but it was important from the point of view of health and social and pension insurance and things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, these first seven pages of the document, do they contain your signature and your stamp of the CSB Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the middle, it is my signature and that's the stamp too. And to the left is the signature of every chief of every organisational unit at the time. And on the right-hand side, the person who was actually paying these amounts out.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you say that this person was in charge, does it pertain to the month of April or to the time when this document was actually written?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document -- the period of time when the document was actually written.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And when was that, if can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the month of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Please look at the next three pages of the document that start with FI20-0008 and then further on. Those are the ERN numbers. We see that there are two signatures, that there is a small stamp. Can you tell us something about these documents.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These documents are not signed by the centre chief and there is also no stamp of the CSB centre Doboj. I wouldn't know whose stamp that is because it is smeared, and also I cannot recognise the one on the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, in this document, on all three pages, we see lists of names. Is any among those persons, as far as you can remember, an employee of the Doboj CSB? Or was any of them an employee of the CSB Doboj at the time?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recognise any name on this list as an employee of the CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P2334, MFI. It's tab 24G. It's Prosecution tab 24G.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is also a document that was shown to you by the Prosecution and you commented on it. Is this a CSB document or not?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a document originating in the public security station in Doboj, and it is signed by its chief. You can see it in the lower right-hand corner. It was the chief of the public security station, Obren Petrovic; it's his signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, my learned colleague, Ms. Korner, pointed to number 15, a person named Veljko Solaja. You gave your explanation, but I don't think it is entirely clear in the transcript. Could you tell us once again: What is your explanation that the fact that Veljko Solaja is on this list?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the period that we are discussing now, there was no crime department within the Doboj CSB and all the inspectors whose names are on this list worked, at that time, in the crime department of the public security station in Doboj. Later on, Inspector Solaja arrived in that department when it was being re-established, sometime by the end of July. But during this period, they all worked in the crime department of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When you Inspector Solaja arrived in the department, what was the organ? Was it the Department of the Security Services Centre? Is that what happened in July?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The following document is 2331, MFI; 24F, Prosecution tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you were also shown this document. Can you tell us whose document it is, in your opinion; who signed it; and did any of the persons listed here work in the Security Services Centre in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document speaks for itself. This is police detachment staff of the public security station in Doboj. And the document is signed by the chief of the Doboj public security station, Obren Petrovic. All persons listed here from number 1 to number 11 worked at the relevant time in the public security station in Doboj. That was their place of employment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, can you remember, payment of salaries in the Doboj CSB in 1992, from what point on was it carried out, performed by the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The flow of funds from the Ministry of Interior began approximately at the time when the ministry itself was constituted in the field. And that is end of July, beginning of August.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And up to that point, as far as you know, what was the source of funds for salaries for the lists that we have been looking at?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the funds were secured by the Crisis Staff and that -- that the payments of salaries went through the accountancy service of the CSB Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P2326, MFI. It's Prosecution tab 77.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, you remember that the Prosecution showed you this document and asked you to comment on it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, during cross-examination, Ms. Korner asked you to explain this document and to tell -- to tell us what the abbreviations I-LP and I-LR stand for. But there is something that you were not asked to comment on. The eight persons that we see here, are they members of the CSB or SJB in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are the individual lists of killed and wounded persons submitted by public security stations in the area covered by the centre. Those lists were then collated and forwarded to the Ministry of the Interior. We can find the names of both active and reserve members of police in those lists of killed and wounded persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When we talk specifically about these persons here, to which public security station do they belong?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that they belong to a number of stations. Some of them belong to the Doboj public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have P2340. That's tab 100.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Sorry, before we move on, in light of the witness's answer, could we have a specific question addressed to him about the fact that the document itself says: "The following members of the Doboj SJB." That seems to be contrary to his answer, where he said they came from several stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Indeed. Thank you, Mr. Hannis. This is my omission.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The document says: "Members of the Doboj public security service who were killed or wounded." Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. It is also my omission. The whole list pertains to the Doboj public security station. I apologise. I was trying to recognise the names, but now I see that we have it written here quite clearly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have P2340. May we have the second page.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, you remember that Ms. Korner showed you this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this your document? Maybe we can show the last page, page 4, which contains the signature.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would like to see the signature. Yes, that's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, the persons listed here and we see 119 names, plus seven, which gives a total of 126. That is, seven killed and 119 wounded. To whom did they belong?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This list contains the names of members belonging to all the public security station covered by the area of the CSB in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this a unified, collated list that you submitted to the Ministry of the Interior which contains information on the MUP members who had been killed or wounded?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is a collated list that covers all the public security stations that belong to our CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does it contain the names of both active and reserve policemen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It contains the names of both active and reserve policemen who had been killed or wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show to the witness P2333, MFI. It's tab 106. I would like to ask the Prosecution who -- Ms. Korner showed a printed coloured version to the witness, and maybe we could provide the same version now so that the witness can follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, you remember that you spoke to Ms. Korner about this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I remember it well, you said that did you not recognise this book.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I also can't read what's written on the front page on this white piece of paper.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Judging by its contents, are you able to say, after you've taken a look at the contents of the book, for instance, page 2 and onwards, are you able to say what this is? What is your opinion?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it's a log-book from the public security station in Doboj. If I look at the columns and the contents of the columns, then I think that that's what it is.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a book coming from the public security station in Doboj. Judging from what I can see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could you speak more slowly. Actually I have to repeat my question because I forgot to switch on the microphone. Does this document have anything to do with the CSB in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is a document originating in the public security station in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 20101. That's Prosecution tab 105. I'm not sure whether the Prosecution has this document in a printed form. Thank you very much. You remember, Mr. Bjelosevic, that Ms. Korner showed you this document as well.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that you did not recognise this document either.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not recognise it. And I hadn't seen it until it was shown to me here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the second page and the third page. And tell us what is your opinion? What is it? What kind of document is it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a log-book recording all daily events.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think that the position of Ms. Korner was that this document originated in the public security station in Bosanski Samac.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we take a look at the columns, we can maybe establish it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Take a look at the places mentioned.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I'm looking for. Yes, the places mentioned here belonged, at the time, to the public security station, Bosanski Samac, Obudovac, Pelagicevo. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the witness please be shown 65 ter 20100 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Mr. Zecevic, it's that time for the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Oh. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So perhaps we can take it now before you move on to something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is ushered in, may the record reflect that Stanisic's Defence is joined by Ms. Suzana Mohr. And I would like to tell the Trial Chamber that I have two more issues and I think roughly 20 minutes. But Mr. Hannis, during the break we discussed, and I need to return to a previous document to comment with the witness. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I, Your Honours?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, during the break, Mr. Hannis asked me to comment on something with you. It's document 2333, MFI. That's tab 106 in the OTP binder. That's the first document you were looking at.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this one. The first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please go to page with ERN number 06651339. The numbers are in the upper right corner. It's a lengthy document, and I apologise, because I'm not sure of the page. It's probably page 20 in e-court. 06651339.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The first date is 3 December 1992.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've found it. 3-9.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see it on the screens too. The sequential number is 136, the first one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, entries 137, 138, and 140 in the column for the place, all read "Orasije Doboj".

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Can you first explain whether Orasije belongs to the Doboj municipality and why, according to you, this can be found in this document.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Orasije is a populated place in the suburbs of Doboj, or, rather, a neighbourhood. And it belongings to the town of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Does this have anything to do with the Orasije municipality in the north of Bosnia-Herzegovina which belongs to the Samac SJB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It is totally unrelated. This is part of Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown document 65 ter 20100. It's tab 104 in the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] While we are waiting for that document, the last document you showed the witness before the break, Prosecutor's binder tab 105.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: The daily event log-book has not been tendered. Not by -- not by you, not by the OTP. If that's how it should be ... ?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, this is one of the fresh documents, the fresh evidence. That is why I don't intend to tender or rely on this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, do you remember that this document, too, was shown to you by Ms. Korner? Unfortunately, we can only see it on the screens.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I remember it by this torn label.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I believe that during the cross-examination you commented on this label and what it says but it wasn't recorded. Could you please tell us more about this.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says "crime register for," and then there's a list of years, 1988, 1989, 1990, 1991, 1992, 1993, 1994, 1995 with the addition "until July".

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And in the upper left corner of the label we see something. Can you read it and explain to us what this is about?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Although it's damaged, I can see that it says OSUP Doboj, which stands for Municipal Secretariat of Internal Affairs, Doboj. That was the old name of the SJB. It's synonymous.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Is this a document of the Doboj SJB?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the meantime, the name was changed. It was no longer the OSUP but it became the SJB. Territorially, however, the same territory was covered.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Bjelosevic, I'll move onto another topic. On page 21.014 and 15 of the transcript, Ms. Korner commented on the situation concerning Mr. Karlo Grgic with you. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And on the following page, I believe, 21.015, she asked you: "Did you talk to Predrag Radulovic about Karlo Grgic?" And your answer was: "Predrag Radulovic, I don't know if I ever met him during the war." Then she interrupted you so that the rest of your reply was not recorded. Let me ask you, Mr. Bjelosevic: You confirm that you saw Radulovic in Teslic on 1 July 1992, so that is not in dispute. Did you see Predrag Radulovic before the 1st of July, 1992? But only in 1992, not before?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the war - that is, from the beginning of May till the end of June - I don't think that I met him at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Could the document Ms. Korner showed to you be shown again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's P1337, which is under tab 20 in the OTP binder.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, do you remember that Ms. Korner showed you this document, which is a report?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's turn the page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This report is dated 17 May 1992.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Once she showed you this report, Ms. Korner quoted Mr. Radulovic's assertions to you, which he made during his testimony before this Court on the 26th of May. If you remember, we were unable to establish the time-period -- the relevant time-period. I must ask you once more: When did you learn - if you remember, of course - of the death of Karlo Grgic and Ilija Tipura?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I learned of these two deaths on two separate occasions, but I could not give you the exact dates. I'm really making an effort to give you at least an approximate date, but I seem unable to.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you the following question. Did you know about these events in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I think that I didn't know either in May or in June. I think I only learned of this later, but I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on page 10.000 -- no. 10.800 of the transcript of the 26th of May, 2010, there's a reference and I'll ask you about some things that the witness said in his testimony. Do you know a person by the name of Mile Bosnjak?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember some people with that last name, but I'm not sure that anybody's first name was Mile.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mile Bosnjak should be an old and experienced police officer.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, then that's the one who worked in Bijeljina, if I remember well. I think that he was on operative duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And where did he work, did you say?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did he work in Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember a man by that name and surname in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Korner put to you something that we can -- something that we can find on page 21.015 that you met Radulovic in the latter half of May 1992 and that Mr. Radulovic informed you of his alleged knowledge of the deaths of Karlo Grgic and Ilija Tipura. Let me introduce you to the context. You said a minute ago that you do not remember meeting Mr. Radulovic. But Mr. Radulovic said on that day when he met you at the CSB Doboj in your office, that he was stopped --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Your Honour, I object. I think this is contrary to your previous order on the -- the rules that we deal with in asking questions and this is not a proper form of asking a question, to comment on something some other witness has said here. I object to the form of the question. It needs to be put to him in a different manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: You can rephrase, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, do you know that Mile Bosnjak was in Doboj in May?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really cannot remember who Mile Bosnjak is. But when you said that he was an experienced police officer, then I remembered that I saw an older, experienced police officer in Bijeljina. But I don't remember anybody by that name in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, on page 10.801, which records Mr. Radulovic's testimony given on 26th May, 2010, the name of Milan Maric is mentioned. Do you know that name?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Did you meet Milan Maric in May 1992 in your office?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Most certainly not. Milan Maric was secretary of the OSUP. But, as far as I know, in the month of May, and even the -- the months before and after May, he wasn't even in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, do you know a person by the name of Drago Paravac?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I know a number of people whose last name is Paravac, but I don't remember who Drago Paravac could be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Drago Paravac should be a politician from Doboj. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no such politician in Doboj.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Page 10.802, the testimony given on 26th May 2010. This is for reference. "Do you know Drago Paravac, who had his office in the building across the road from the SUP and was a politician from Doboj?"

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot even suppose where an office across the road from the SUP could be, because there was a residential building -- or, rather, several buildings. They also had some shops, there was some shops in those buildings but those shops were not offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Drago Paravac was ever the president of the Executive Board of Doboj?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That was Boro Paravac, not Drago Paravac.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Boro Paravac. Did he have an office opposite the CSB Doboj SUP building in May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The municipality building is in a completely different street. Behind the park out there. It's about 200 metres away, I think, from the police building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, it was asserted here that during that meeting that you do not recall -- just a moment, please. When you were told that Karlo Grgic was killed, and Professor Dr. Ilija Tipura, it was alleged that you had said, I cannot do anything about that. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. Had there been that kind of a discussion, I certainly would have remembered it. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, after what happened on the 1st of July in Teslic, you said that you did not talk to Mr. Radulovic for a while, because, if I understood you correctly, you were angry at him. How long was it that you were not on speaking terms with him?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A few years. I cannot be more specific than that. But perhaps even up until 2000, 2001, something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After 2001, did you talk to him?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: During these conversations, was this discussion from May 1992 ever mentioned to you?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, since we've touched upon Teslic briefly, let us clarify that as well. 839 is the P number. The tab is -- I don't know. I assume that it's Prosecution tab 251.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you know --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, this was a document that was not on the Defence list of documents to be used until I got an e-mail yesterday afternoon about 2.45 after court was over. I want to reiterate my objection to this late addition; this is something the Defence must have known about before then that they'd want to use with the witness. Also, I need a reference now as to what part of the cross-examination this arises from.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just been informed that it is 21161. That's the reference. Ms. Korner was commenting on the situation in Teslic with the witness. In that context, she mentions that this document, P839; that is, Mr. Markocevic's statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, it was asserted that -- it was asserted by Ms. Korner that as one reads this statement -- actually, do you know, Mr. Bjelosevic, that Mr. Markocevic and another person came to see you one evening in Doboj but they didn't find you. This was sometime in mid-June 1992.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember. It is possible that someone was looking for me and that I wasn't there, but I do not remember having received that kind of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Markocevic and another person had a meeting with Savic and Culibrk because you were not there?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I know -- actually, later on I heard that the president of the municipality from Teslic came at some point and some MPs as well and they were the commanders of the operations group. I was not there at that time. I know that on one occasion, again the president of the municipality, Mr. Perisic came, and I cannot remember who was with him, and I know that we met up and they asked me, because I think they knew that I was at the forward command post of the 1st Krajina Corps, whether I could help them with regard to the following. To having the Teslic military brigade be assigned to logistics of the Logistics Base of the 1st Krajina Corps. I promised that I would help them with that, that I would talk to General Talic, and I told them to address General Talic directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On that occasion, did you talk about the Mice and about the situation in Teslic at all?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On that occasion nothing was mentioned with regard to that particular topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic. You were shown document -- MFI document from tab 57, 2342. You confirmed that it was your document from the 8th of September, 1992. You're going to get it now. You'll see it on your screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You remember that this document was shown to you. This is a proposal for the appointment of chief, commander and head of the crime investigation service. It was sent to the ministry, and Dusan Kuzmanovic, Predrag Markocevic and Marinko Djukic were your proposed candidates for these posts.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Tell us, Mr. Bjelosevic, what was the reason for you to make this proposal to the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Objection, Your Honour. I'm not sure how this arises out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, the suggestion by Ms. Korner was that -- can the witness take the headphones off. The suggestion by Ms. Korner was that these people -- these persons who were proposed by Mr. Bjelosevic for these posts have been involved in the -- in a Mice incident and all the incidents in Teslic. And she showed the document. He confirmed it is his document. I'm just inquiring why did he propose these people to the posts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you can, could you please explain to us what your -- you were motivated by to put up these candidates for these posts in the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These three persons who were proposed for these posts; namely, chief, commander and head of the crime investigation service, held those positions up until those events that occurred concerning the Mices in Teslic. Let me just say one thing. After that incident, on that same day, when I asked Kuzmanovic why he had not reported about what had happened there, he said that that was for reasons pertaining to personal safety. And both Markocevic and Djukic agreed with that. After all of these things that had happened, they came to speak to me. They also wrote a note, a rather extensive one explaining what had happened there. They were jobless. They were motivated - at least that's what they stated - to help to a maximum in shedding more light on what had happened in that period of time in Teslic. And, on the basis of that, I made my decision, since formally, according to the law, the Teslic station was supposed to be within the CSB of Doboj, I decided to make this proposal that they be appointed to these posts and that they really help shed more light on what had happened. May I note that they were not involved in the investigation that had taken place until then in any way. They were not to be blamed in any way. May I add one more thing. Afterwards, I proposed Mr. Marinko Djukic to be appointed inspector in the police in Doboj. Later on, he was appointed to that position. And I assess the results he achieved in that period of time as exceptional. His performance during that period of time was exceptional, in my view.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bjelosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, in light of that, may this exhibit now have the MFI removed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Do you have an observation -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm perfectly accepting this document to be admitted into evidence. However, I'm not sure if this document should be given a P number, which he already has, in light of our submissions in the future. So if -- if that is okay with -- with my learned friend, I would propose that this document be admitted as one 1D document and I can offer it for its admission. I know it's -- it might be too formalistic but what I'm afraid is that we might be creating an exception in this respect. But on the -- on reflection, if I do not object, then -- then surely there is no -- there is no point that this -- that this stays MFI'd. I understand, I'm sorry. So it can be removed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, I would ask the MFI be removed and it keep the P number. In the Prosecution case we had a number of documents that were presented by the Prosecution [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... and had 1D numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I was caught off guard.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, just for the record, this is Exhibit P2342.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bjelosevic, just two more things briefly and then we'll be done. 65 ter 20018 was shown to you. That is Prosecution tab 65, although this document had been announced by the Defence as well. You will see it in a moment or two on your screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have page 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Remember that you commented on this document, and Ms. Korner was suggesting certain things in relation to your attitude towards the military and the police. Remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, during 1992, was there a competition for vacant posts in the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. People were supposed to apply and then they were supposed to enrol in courses in order to train to become policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These persons, once they complete a course, would they become employed in the Ministry of the Interior only then?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Those who would successfully complete this training would then be employed as policemen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To the best of your recollection, these 14 persons, did they apply when this vacancy was announced and that involved training for policemen?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Because that is what this document seems to show.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this letter, it says that selection was made amongst the many persons who had applied.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: These persons, at that time, that is to say, the end of September 1992, were they serving in the armed forces? Were they members of the military?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is why this letter requested they be relieved of their duties so that they could be sent to this course.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I am being told that this document is 1D471. Mr. Bjelosevic, we've come to the very end. On page -- just a moment, please. Ms. Korner showed you document P2339, MFI; that's Prosecution tab 84A.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The transcript reference is 21.164.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that you commented on this document?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is excerpts from the record. I believe that you pointed to Ms. Korner that your diary contains the entry for the 6th of January, 1993 that relates to this document. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have 1D065464.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Could the counsel please repeat the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D065464. That was the document -- that was the last document to be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, during the examination of Ms. Korner, on the page that I quoted and onwards, a question arose: Who suggested that there were problems in the Doboj SJB? You then requested closed session in order to answer that question. Do you still stand by that? Do you think that it should be answered in private session?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I ask again for a page reference, since the one I heard before doesn't seem to be in the right spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 21180. Excuse me, 21118. Your Honour, can we move to private session so that the witness can answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. But before we do that, why do I - and my memory may be entirely faulty here and you will correct me if I'm wrong. But why is my recollection that when this arose when Ms. Korner was cross-examining that the issue had resolved itself in such a way that it was unnecessary to move into private session. Or am I confusing this something with another Teslic matter?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, you're not confusing, Your Honour. That is correct. Ms. Korner objected to going into private session and then we did go into private session for a very short period of time, witness gave the answer, and then Ms. Korner said, I don't want to pursue this anymore. Mr. Zecevic will take over in his re-direct. And then you can provide the answers. I am fine with your answer as it is. And then Ms. Korner asked that we return back to the open session. But now, as we are returning to the subject matter which the witness suggested needs the private session because the mentioning of some families --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: I remember the reason given. Yes. So we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: And we take the break, to return in 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: So, Mr. Zecevic, you have completed your re-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. And I do have objection but I'm waiting for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- sorry. Microphone wasn't on. I was about do ask Mr. Hannis whether he wishes to expand on the objection that he began to formulate just before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, I would make a request. It's primarily a follow-up on a question that Judge Delvoie asked in relation to the private session testimony about this document. It's certainly I think something within your ability to permit. And it relates also to the position I take about this document which is currently marked MFI. I may seek to remove the MFI, but my questions relate to that too because it goes to the authenticity of this document and the truthfulness of this document, and for that reason, I would ask to be permitted to ask about five minutes' worth of questions about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, if I may make things easier for Mr. Hannis, we do not challenge the authenticity of this document. And the provenance of the document. Ms. Korner explained where they got the document. I explained to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Could you remind me, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Ms. Korner said that they received the document on Monday and it was brought by the investigator of the Office of the Prosecutor. I confirmed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] Sorry, the witness can be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I brought to Your Honours' attention that I discussed the document previously with the witness. So there is no problem whatsoever in that respect concerning the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I oppose to the document being introduced because -- because I think that's a fresh evidence, and that -- it is MFI'd pending our submissions which I understand will happen on Thursday, when Ms. Korner arrives, about the -- the fresh -- the fresh evidence, which was -- which was MFI'd during the cross-examination of Ms. Korner. Now, as concerning the request to re-open the cross-examination by Mr. Hannis, I would like to remind Your Honours of what Ms. Korner said on the transcript on the 23rd. Line -- page 21124: "Q. Now, Mr. Bjelosevic, in one sentence why do you want to explain this in private at the suggestion, I note, of Mr. Zecevic? "A. Because it will have to do with private matters" and so on and so on. "Q. The only question I want to ask you, Mr. Petrovic" - and it was a mistake - "I have already asked you was it you that said it was objectionable for him to have retained two Muslim workers. That's all I want to know; nothing else. What requires you to go into private matters?" Now, any further explanation -- now the witness says, "No. But I wish to explain this, how things went at the meeting, in private session. But it seems to me that that is not being allowed, how this wording came to be -- "Q. Right, well ... any further explanation," that's Ms. Korner, "Mr. Zecevic who wants to take it from you, can in-chief [sic]. My question is simply that: Are you prepared to say who it was who made that remark in open session? "A. I would leave this for private session." Therefore, Ms. Korner specifically had the opportunity to ask the witness, but she said no, I don't need. I just want this answer and nothing else. Therefore, that -- that is it -- that is the gist of my objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Zecevic. Mr. Hannis, although you have formulated -- I should say reformulated your application premised on the question asked by the Bench, the -- it really arises out of this area that came out in the re-examination. And as Mr. Zecevic has correctly pointed out, the Prosecution, in the person of Ms. Korner, although probably she had no idea what this evidence could have been, having had the opportunity, chose not to pursue it. So procedurally, we do have a concern as to whether the Prosecution can properly be permitted to now explore this area, which it tactically chose not to, for whatever reason, when the opportunity arose.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I could -- I could make an argument that Ms. Korner perhaps, given her experience with this witness up to that point, felt she'd rather not go into an area where she didn't know what the answer might be but I guess I would fall back on the second part of my application where I say that what I want to do is follow up on a question raised by the Bench. Now, in one of the other trials I was in the standard practice was for the Judges to wait until all the examination was done and then ask their questions. Of course, I think we lawyers find it helpful for the judges to intervene whenever they want, because they can clarify something as it's happening. But when the Judges ask questions at the end, if it raises something new, then parties on both sides typically are given the opportunity to expand. This came at the very end of his testimony, and Judge Delvoie asks a question which, I think, raises an issue that I think bears touching on with this witness while he's here. And if Your Honours have no more questions, and you decide you're not going to allow me to ask anything further, I have to live with that. If you have any further questions, I may be able to tie it with your remaining questions. I'll abide by your ruling, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
