utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: -- the answers which the explanation of the statement which, as I recall the witness's acceptance is, at best infelicitous, are such that the -- it does strongly invite some further explanation than we have had heretofore and we would permit you to ask further questions on that. But, of course, Mr. Zecevic would have a right to come back on that. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, just one matter. I think we need to go back to the private session and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Insofar as it is possible, it seems to me, to explore the area without calling name, I don't know if that is necessary. Mr. Hannis, can you avoid using names.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I did not intend to use the names of -- that were the reason that we went into private session for. I will refer to the name of the SJB chief in Doboj, but ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: To be on the safe side perhaps we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, I want to go back to something you told us on Thursday, last Thursday, if I'm not wrong. It's 19 May, page 3422. It's about the war station in Osinja, if I pronounce that correctly in the Derventa municipality and you were asked by the Prosecutor, in April, was that police station entirely manned by Serb members of the MUP or reserve MUP? And your answer was: "I don't know, but because Osinja, and neighbouring villages are inhabited only by Serbs, I assume that probably the manpower was also of Serb ethnicity. That's my assumption." You remember that answer? So if I got you right, what you're saying here is that the mono-ethnic composition of that war station was a coincidence resulting from the ethnic composition of the population. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: That was not the case in the Doboj SJB, I suppose. There were -- that's -- that's a mixed population, and -- I mean the territory is mixed. And the police station then was manned by Serbs and Muslims alike; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And other ethnicities as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Other ethnicities as well. Indeed. But that didn't prevent that station to be -- or that SJB to be mono-ethnic somewhere in April -- in April, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in April.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... when was it then? When did all the Serb employees, except for those who had extramarital affairs within the service, left? When did they left -- when did they leave? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I think Your Honour made a slip of the tongue. You're referring not to Serb employees; you're referring to Muslim employees [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It was recorded 68, 6, Serb employees.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: I'm sorry about that.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The differentiation was carried out sometime at the beginning of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. And they left, you told us. Is that a general term, in respect of the reason why they left? Was it -- did they leave out of their free will?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, we should be clear about this. Let me explain. A number of people left the service already in April, and I'm talking about all ethnicities here. They saw that the war came to the area, and a number of them left out of fear already in April. At the beginning of May, a number of the members of the service left deliberately towards the area of Tesanj, the area of Gracanica, et cetera. I want to emphasise that one mobile communications centre, in a car, was driven away before the 1st of May by a reserve member who had been activated by the state security. I think his name was Mirzo Kunalic [phoen]. So a certain kind of differentiation was already going on. The equipment was already being taken away. And the preparations were already under way for the new system of functioning. However, after the 3rd of May, as far as I know, members of the service simply did not come to work in the public security station or the centre. And I already explain when this process began, how it went, and what was the purpose of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Nobody was forced out -- was forced to leave the service.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know of a single decision terminating employment for someone in this way. Or that somebody was turned away from -- turned away when he or she appeared for work. I know of not a single case like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Or being arrested while still in the service.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, people were arrested or brought, not when they were at the official premises, because that's not where they were, as far as I know. People were arrested elsewhere, in the street, or in their apartments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So including policemen? No policemen were arrested on the premises, or because of they were still in the service?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably a number of them were arrested in the night between the 2nd and the 3rd of May. And according to what I heard about later on, about the persons who were detained and who had been members of the service before, it's not that they arrived for work and then they were arrested. Rather, it happened outside official premises. They were various reasons for that. I used to inquire about the reasons, and, for instance, they were cases when people were called to return the keys, or some of them took part in organisation of paramilitary formations. These are the things that I learned when I was informed that some members of the service were detained.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: But then I -- if -- if nobody was forced out and particularly nobody of non-Serb ethnicity, I still have difficulty to understand, even if it is a cover-up, why the reason -- the criticism to a station commander, or chief, could officially be covering up what really happened but -- could officially be that he retained Muslim employees within the -- within the force, within the service. Because it sounds a little bit like calling somebody a murderer to cover up that he is a thief. Don't you agree?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I understood your comparison. I attempted to explain the essence of this case and to say that, in the end, it simply amounted to rather unfortunate wording that was used to explain something that had nothing to do with it. And I remind you that three persons were involved in this, not two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Now I want to come back to General Talic's order, two orders, about Derventa, and more, in particular, his order to another station to send policemen to Derventa to do the policing over there. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. However, you misquoted the name. It wasn't General Talic. It was Colonel Lisica, if I understood the topic that you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. That could very well be. We'll see. Asked by Mr. Zecevic, you answered that this particular order -- it could very well be Colonel Lisica. That this particular order was given in accordance with his powers. Could you be more precise? In accordance with what law would that be? The Law on Resubordination?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the Law on All People's Defence. And the Law on Armed Forces. They are the two laws, and both of them contain grounds and bestow such powers on the commanders of this and higher rank.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Does that mean that this -- such an order would be considered as an order to -- resubordination order and, therefore, an order to carry out combat activities?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the order to carry out combat activities for a particular segment of the police station in Derventa. However, since the commander has the power to engage all the forces in his zone of responsibility, he ensured that Derventa would be supplied with some other forces as well. And that's when he ordered that police forces from Prnjavor should be engaged as well. I assumed had there not been this urgency, that he would not have sent the police forces from Prnjavor to the front line and since it took some time for them to arrive, he decided to engage also those who were closer to the line of hostilities. And then, subsequently, the first group was engaged in carrying out security-related tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Just an intervention in the transcript for the clarity. It is recorded 72, 1 that he would not. In fact the witness said that he would have. Had not been the matter of this urgency he would have sent the police forces from Prnjavor to the front line. But since it took them some time to arrive he decided to engage those who were close to the line of hostilities. May the witness can slowly again repeat his answer, because it's not -- it's not clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Would you do that, Mr. Bjelosevic?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I assume that because of the urgency of the situation, Colonel Lisica decided to engage the police from Derventa at the front line, because they were closer to the front line. I also assume that he would have decided to engage the police from Prnjavor at the front line if he had more time -- if he had had more time. I think that it was exactly the urgency of the situation that made him do what he did. However, he also wanted to ensure that Derventa would not be left without any police, and that's why he ordered that the Prnjavor police should arrive in Derventa, and carry out security-related tasks there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Well, that's -- that's precisely my question, that second -- that second order, the order for the Prnjavor policemen to go to Derventa to do police work, can that be considered as a resubordination order to carry out combat activities; and, if not, could Colonel Lisica give such an order?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He did have the powers to do that. It wouldn't be considered a resubordination. It would be considered engagement, this thing related to the police from Prnjavor. And if he needed to do that, he would probably have used them at the front line as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Thank you. My last question is this: During the war, lots of people were -- who had performed their military duty before the war were mobilised and served in the army during the war. That's what war is more or less about, isn't it? Now, my question is: Would the information about the service during wartime be reflected in their military booklet?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information is entered into the military booklet, according to the wartime assignment. Which means, if somebody had a wartime assignment in the military, then this wartime assignment, in this particular unit is entered into the booklet. If somebody had his wartime assignment in the Republic of police force, then that's what is entered into the booklet. At the same time, there was work obligation. So people who had work obligation in certain companies, for them, the information entered was the job that they performed. Am I being clear enough? I'm not quite sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Thank you. But then I wonder why don't we see anything of this reflected in your military booklet? Unless I got it wrong.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My wartime assignment was in the MUP organs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... So we should see it.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this wartime assignment remained throughout.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So we should find that in your military booklet. Because that's what you just told us.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: And is it in your military booklet?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, Your Honours, I could be of assistance. It's -- it's the last page of his military booklet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Was it showed to us? Not yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I'm afraid not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I failed to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So my question is not as stupid as it looked.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: No, no, it's not stupid at all. It's my failure, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: So if I understand it well now, what you're saying is your wartime, one's wartime assignment is in the booklet and if that wartime assignment is something else than the military, for instance, the MUP, police, and within that wartime assignment, there is, for a certain period of time, resubordination, you are -- one is resubordinated to the military for combat activities, then you will not find that in one's military booklet. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If it is about the principle of resubordination, of being engaged there, then nothing changes here on this side. The wartime assignment remains as it was originally assigned. But that is not an obstacle for a person to be engaged in defence activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Okay. Seems a little bit odd to me, because you can be the most heroic soldier within that period that is not reflected in your military booklet. But so be it, and now I understand what you're telling us. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If Your Honours have no further questions I have one question based on one of Judge Delvoie's questions about whether any police were arrested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Witness, at page 69, Judge Delvoie, line 17 was asking you about whether any non-Serbs were arrested, any -- any policemen. I want to ask you, do you remember a policeman named Mirza Lisinovic and whether or not he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that Mirza Lisinovic was performing the duty of the operative duty officer in the night between the 2nd and the 3rd of May, and that's when he was detained. However, he was released immediately the day after.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You're sure he wasn't detained for two weeks and that you were the ones to whom he was told to hand over his papers and keys?

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely not. I certainly did not say that to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Okay.

utterances.speaker: ANDRIJA BJELOSEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, however, how long he spent in the detention. I spoke to Mirza Lisinovic later on. I don't know how many days after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Bjelosevic, we thank you for your attendance before the Tribunal. You are now released as a witness, and we wish you a safe journey back to your home. The Court has some other matters with which to deal, so the usher will escort you from the courtroom at this point. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I would be glad if my testimony would help you to reach the right decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The Chamber has a very short oral ruling to deliver and then it has a question to pose to counsel for the accused Stanisic. The ruling is as follows. On the 19th of May, the Stanisic Defence orally requested the Trial Chamber to preclude the Prosecution from introducing fresh evidence during the course of the Defence case, the Prosecution having already had the opportunity to do so during its own case. The Defence relied for its request on the decision dated 26 February 2009 by the Appeals Chamber at the Prlic et al case. The Prosecution asserted that the Defence was re-arguing the point. Having considered the jurisprudence, and independent of how the Chamber may rule on the other pending matter before it on the application of Rule 66(B) in due course, the Trial Chamber sees no reason to distinguish this situation from that in Prlic and will follow the Appeals Chamber on this matter by evaluating any such fresh evidence on a case-by-case basis. The Defence motion is therefore denied. The question that we have for counsel for Stanisic is this, and isn't a question in which we are expecting an answer immediately but at some point, possibly as early as tomorrow, counsel may wish to address it, and it is this. And because we are in open session I'm not going to give the details what I'm saying but, referring to the proofing note that we have received in respect of the witness who is about to -- to give evidence, and the very last paragraph indicating an application about the mode of testimony of the witness, insofar as, on the face of it, it appears to what is indicated at paragraph 18 of the proofing note, we wonder what is the -- how -- how -- how this issue -- how the application would arise because, on the face of it, it is something which is not relevant. As I have said, we have alerted counsel and no doubt we will get the response tomorrow or at some future time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: By all means, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes. So we take the adjournment, to reconvene in this courtroom tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
